problem: AgriVLN treats each instruction as an independent episode, ignoring past experience in the same scene. With the low 0.38m camera height, the robot sees its immediate surroundings well but lacks global spatial context (SR only 0.47 on A2A).
motivation: In agricultural settings workers often repeat the same instruction in the same scene, as humans do when they build subconscious spatial memory from a first trip. Reusing earlier experience could provide the global context the low camera view lacks.
key_idea: Reconstruct the scene in 3D with VGGT from frames of a previous run, render frontal/oblique 2D views as a stored spatial memory, and feed these images to the VLM-based AgriVLN agent to guide its decisions in later runs.
insight: Adding spatial memory raises SR in every scene type (Table 2) and on low-complexity tasks (SR 0.58->0.66), but gains fade on tasks with 4 or more subtasks (SR stays at 0.14, NE 7.53->8.26). A single rendering perspective is enough: hybrid frontal+oblique is not better (SR 0.53 vs 0.54) and costs about 18% more input tokens. Oblique helps on flat forest terrain where objects occlude each other in the frontal view; frontal is as good or better on uneven mountain terrain.
method: Spatial Understanding: uniformly samples q=10 frames from the earlier camera stream and feeds them to VGGT, which outputs a 3D reconstruction in GLB format.
Spatial Memory: trimesh renders the reconstruction as an RGB point cloud, and two 2D views (frontal at 0-5 degrees, oblique at 40-50 degrees, 360x640) are saved in a Spatial Memory Bank.

Base model integration: the SUM module sits between visual input and decision making in AgriVLN. At each step the VLM receives the memory image(s) (frontal, oblique or both), the subtask list, the camera frames and a prompt.
Subtask List module (from AgriVLN): decomposes the instruction into subtasks.
Output parsing: each step's output has four tagged sections. Regex extracts the action (FORWARD / LEFT ROTATE / RIGHT ROTATE / STOP), a spatial-understanding thought and a decision thought.
Termination: an episode ends on STOP, on deviation from the label action sequence, or at the step limit.

setting.backbone: AgriVLN base model (VLM accessed via official API, frozen) + VGGT (frozen) for reconstruction
setting.observation: front-facing monocular RGB (0.38m camera height) + stored rendered 3D-reconstruction images from a prior run of the same scene
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD / LEFT ROTATE / RIGHT ROTATE / STOP
setting.simulator: A2A benchmark (recorded agricultural videos), no standard simulator
setting.privileged: pre-exploration of the same scene (earlier camera stream used to build the spatial memory)

numbers.extra: requires a prior pre-exploration run to build the spatial memory; oblique view
numbers.evidence: Table 1 row #7 (whole A2A): SR 0.54, NE 2.93, ISR 2.08 / 2.90

numbers.extra: pre-exploration; hybrid view, about 18% more input tokens

numbers_note: The A2A benchmark has no official split names in the text, so 'test' is used for the full benchmark. The metrics are also reported for the low-complexity and high-complexity portions; the oblique low-complexity SR is 0.66, NE 2.26; the high-complexity SR is 0.42, NE 3.64.
results: On A2A, SUM-AgriVLN raises SR from 0.47 (AgriVLN) to 0.54, above DILLM-VLN (0.36) and SIA-VLN (0.31), while NE goes from 2.91m to 2.93m. It does not beat DILLM-VLN on NE (2.60m), and it remains far below humans (SR 0.87).
limitations: Only static scenes are supported; dynamic objects cause ghosting in the 3D reconstruction.
The 2D RGB rendering of the memory loses spatial information, and the method needs a pre-exploration phase for each scene.
Gains vanish on high-complexity tasks (4 or more subtasks), and NE does not improve.
